A scattering-eclipse model fit yields forty-one point eight degrees, plus thirteen point zero, minus fourteen point nine, agreeing with the spectroscopic orbit and challenging prior image readings.
arxiv-2602-23906:
Bora Kargi and two co-authors show that similarity-based image-text retrieval breaks under half-truths, descriptions extended with a plausible but wrong detail. The 2026 paper argues that adding a wrong detail should lower similarity, yet CLIP-style encoders often score the longer, partly false description higher.

On a standard caption set, CLIP picks the correct shorter description only a minority of the time, and it fares worse when the added detail is a relation rather than an object. The authors trace the flaw to contrastive training, which aligns whole sentences without forcing each entity and relation to be grounded. Their fix, CS-CLIP, splits captions into entity and relation units, builds a minimally edited foil for each, and fine-tunes the model to prefer the true unit. Half-truth accuracy rises sharply, with gains on compositional benchmarks too.
arxiv-2602-24006:
Yuhan Lu and two co-authors study Fulde-Ferrell superfluids in an asymmetric three-component Fermi gas. The 2026 paper considers a gas where Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling links the first two components, while contact interaction acts only between the first and third. The gas joins two mechanisms known to stabilize Fulde-Ferrell pairing. The mechanisms are spin-orbit coupling and population imbalance.

Working in two dimensions at zero temperature and minimizing the thermodynamic potential, the authors reveal a new class of composite Fulde-Ferrell superfluids. They emerge when strong spin-orbit coupling creates a double-well structure in momentum space within the lower spin-orbit-coupled band, letting pairing draw on both wells. The paper identifies the key features of these composite states, extending the known landscape of exotic superfluids in multi-component Fermi gases.
arxiv-2603-00106: Zheng and colleagues present DRFF-R2, a real-world multi-scenario dataset of drone radio-frequency signals gathered on a dedicated platform. Its recordings span 26 drone units across 8 distinct models, covering varied flight states, heights, speeds, days and receiver setups. Files sit in seven subsets by scenario and signal mix, under one naming scheme for easy indexing and repeatable analysis. The set supports drone fingerprinting, model recognition, flight-state study, time-varying fingerprint work and interference-aware processing.
arxiv-2603-00206: Medeiros introduces TACIT, a programmatic visual reasoning benchmark with 10 tasks across 6 reasoning domains, from spatial navigation and pattern completion to causal simulation, logic constraints, graph theory and topology. It offers two tracks: a generative track where models produce solution images checked by vision pipelines, and a discriminative track with five-way multiple choice using near-miss distractors. Each distractor breaks exactly one structural constraint, forcing fine-grained reasoning over surface cues. The first release ships 6,000 puzzles with 108,000 PNG images across three resolutions, under the Apache 2 licence.
arxiv-2603-00306: Wang, Dong, and Lei ask when step-by-step chain-of-thought prompting improves reasoning, modelling each reasoning path as a Markov chain of intermediate steps. Their theory singles out transition alignment, whether instances share the same step-to-step transition pattern, as the deciding factor. When transitions stay identical across steps, chain-of-thought needs fewer example trajectories to recover the final decision; when they vary, the benefit can vanish. Noise in intermediate steps further shapes the gain, and synthetic benchmarks built to isolate these factors support the predictions.
arxiv-2603-00406: Bagherian builds an axiomatic base for quantum distance measures on projective Hilbert spaces, bringing scattered measures in quantum information under one roof. From five axioms on invariance, covariance, superposition, entanglement, and measurement context, she shows any valid distance depends only on state overlap. That forces the Fubini-Study metric as the unique canonical geodesic distance. Her frame also orders related distances, adds a complementarity rule, and ties them to telling states apart and to metrology.
arxiv-2603-00806: Blank and three colleagues study condensation in random lattice gases with size-linked steady weights and a math tweak that fades as the system grows. Above a key density, the system splits into an even bulk and a dense phase, forming either one large cluster or many separate clusters at smaller scale. They prove the shift via ensemble math and derive the cluster size spread through size-biased sampling, building on earlier zero-range and inclusion work. Zero-range tests show the results on dense phase scale and spread.
arxiv-2603-01006: Zhang and three colleagues improve REPA training for audio flow matching by picking supervised layers with cause, not depth habit. They find layers richest in semantic content are not always those driving the flow speed, a gap they call Store-Contribute Dissociation. A forward-only gate test scores each layer's causal role, giving sparse picks and tuned weights that beat standard REPA rivals on speech and general audio.
arxiv-2603-01106: Gao and nine colleagues fix two flaws of group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) for multimodal reasoning: thin rewards on hard problems and fading gains when group rewards agree too closely. DIVA-GRPO judges problem hardness from a global view. It samples variants at fitting hardness and works out gains across local and global groups with hardness-weighted scaling. The result eases thin rewards and gain loss with steadier training, beating rival methods on six test sets for speed and scores.
arxiv-2603-01506:
Jianqiang Ren, Lin Liu, and Steven Hoi build a way to turn one photo into a moving 3D head in this 2026 work. Fast, detailed head avatars matter for games, film, meetings, and virtual worlds. A single model should also serve both weak and strong hardware without losing key detail.

Their method, OMG-Avatar, stores the head as Gaussian blobs at several levels of detail. A transformer reads broad face traits, while sampled points add local detail, joined with depth cues to keep overlaps sane. Head and shoulders are built apart, then merged, which fixes a weak spot of older face models. The build takes a fraction of a second, and tests beat prior tools on rebuild quality, acting control, and speed.
arxiv-2603-01806:
Xiong Zhang, Hong Peng, Zhenli He, and colleagues spot anomalous nodes in networks without any labeled examples. Their 2026 work targets bad actors in social and review graphs, such as fake accounts and banned users. A recent method boosts links among normal nodes while cutting links of odd nodes, yet its fixed cutoff misfires.

Their model, GCTAM, splits the cutoff step into contextual and global parts that work together. Contextual truncation lowers the affinity of likely anomalous nodes based on local cues. Global truncation raises affinity among normal nodes, using high-order links the old method ignored. Wide tests on large real graphs show wins over peer methods on most tasks. Gains stand out on two famous review data sets, and the method still finishes on the largest sets where rivals fail.
arxiv-2603-02306:
Adrian Fraser simulates a mixing process inside stars in this 2026 paper. Fingering convection stirs chemicals in star zones where heavy material sits above light material. It matters in red giants and possibly in polluted white dwarfs. Past three-dimensional simulations could not reach the extreme settings found in real stars.

The gap is set by one ratio, comparing viscosity with heat spread, which is tiny in stars. Fraser runs simulations spanning old settings down to true stellar values. A standard mixing model stays consistent with simulations across that whole range. So clashes between that model and observations cannot be blamed on the old gap. Extra physics, not simulation limits, must explain the mismatch.
arxiv-2603-02806:
Jonas von Berg, Adalbert Fono, Massimiliano Datres, and colleagues prove that steady classifiers need to be much bigger than their data. Their 2026 paper defines stability as the average distance from a data point to the model's decision boundary. A larger margin means small input changes rarely flip the answer.

Their bound improves as stability grows, and it needs no smoothness assumptions, covering jagged classifiers too. A direct consequence follows: a model that merely fits its training points with about as many parameters as points must be unstable. Real robustness therefore demands heavy overparameterization. Experiments back the theory, with stability rising alongside model size and tracking test accuracy, while older norm-based measures said little.
arxiv-2603-03206:
Cullen Anderson, Narmeen Oozeer, Foad Namjoo, and colleagues test how poisoned examples can hijack an AI model's steering. Contrastive steering finds a trait direction by comparing the model's inner signals on paired examples. It then shifts those signals along that line at runtime. Safety teams use it a lot, yet nobody had checked how it holds up when the example set is rigged.

A modest share of rigged examples leaves steering mostly intact. Past a clear threshold, though, attackers can plant strong unwanted side effects on purpose. A look at the shapes of distinct attack types points to guards. The weak step is a plain average over many signals. Swapping in a robust form of that average cancels most of the harm.
arxiv-2603-03506:
A M Guzman and M C McDonald hunt for a pattern in detector noise that should exist across columns if it exists at all. Their hunt appears in an instrument report for Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Read noise in bias frames already grows with row number, because dark current builds during readout. Their report checks the column direction for the Wide Field Channel's four amplifiers, across different maintenance periods called anneal cycles.

No column dependence appears. Read noise in the physical prescan regions sits about half an electron lower than in the science arrays, exactly where no readout dark accumulates. Three follow-ups round out the study. Read noise shows no visible trend across an anneal period. Two amplifiers show a brief linear decline across their first science columns. And masking unstable hot pixels lowers the noise of their columns.
arxiv-2603-03606:
Satabdi Das and four colleagues ask blind and visually impaired people what would make photo sharing feel safe. A shared image can accidentally expose sensitive or embarrassing content its owner cannot see, risking privacy and relationships. Their 2026 study tests image obfuscation filters as a pre-sharing shield, with twenty blind and visually impaired participants judging filtered images of varying sensitivity.

Pixelation was the least preferred filter. Other preferences shifted with image type and with the audience, family, friends, or strangers, so no single filter wins everywhere. Across audiences, participants felt more comfortable sharing filtered images than unfiltered ones. The authors turn those patterns into design guidelines for sharing tools that warn and protect without taking control away from the person sharing.
arxiv-2603-03806:
Hanpeng Liu and four colleagues teach a vision model to read many images as one long book, with separators between chapters. Mamba, a state-space architecture, processes sequences causally and efficiently, which suits autoregressive pretraining, but vision versions were stuck with short sequences. Their 2026 method, STAR, inserts an identical separator token before each image, marking where one picture ends and the next begins.

That simple device quadruples the usable input sequence length while keeping every dataset image at its original size. Pretrained the long way, their STAR-B model scores competitively on the standard ImageNet classification benchmark, at the top of the Vision Mamba class. The authors argue the gain comes from finally exploiting the architecture's strength, long-range dependence across a genuinely long visual sequence, rather than from any added parameters.
arxiv-2603-04006: Ariola and others study structural corecursion with standard thought, proving the infinite pigeonhole principle and choice. The authors examine coiteration plus corecursion with the standard callcc operator, giving a computational reading of standard thought. As a use they prove the Infinite Pigeonhole Principle with corecursive control methods. They also build the Axiom of Countable Choice, showing termination by coiteration alone.
arxiv-2603-04106: Hapka and others present optimally tuned multiconfigurational short-range DFT for linear response. Multiconfigurational short-range DFT joins wavefunction theory and DFT, yet unlike single-reference hybrids it lacked grounded rules for setting the range-separation setting. Their tuning scheme enforces exponential density decay, fixing the setting via ionization possible from the smallest eigenvalue of an Extended Koopmans' Theorem matrix. Validation covers static and dynamic polarizabilities for ground-state molecules in full linear response and a random phase variant. Optimal tuning aids polarizabilities over the commonly used universal setting.
arxiv-2603-04206: Gauvain and others present a global high-resolution hydrological model to simulate surface liquid reservoir motion. Surface runoff shapes planetary landscapes, yet global hydrological models often miss the resolution and flexibility for simulating dynamic surface water bodies beyond Earth. Outputs give surface water body extent and depth and spot main drainage pathways via overflow fluxes as runoff indicators.
arxiv-2603-04306: Sun and Kejriwal automate choosing specifications for exponential random graph models of social networks. Such models test tie formation ideas, but researchers now propose, fit, check, and revise models by hand. Forge, their agentic system, takes a network and domain description, proposes hypotheses, builds candidates, and refines the best by goodness of fit. It returns a readable interpretation of the final model, beating the best baseline on 13 of 16 benchmarks and tying the rest. Median goodness of fit improves by 24.8 percent over that baseline.
arxiv-2603-04406: Tan and colleagues train retrieval models to stay faithful to context with CTRL-RAG. Old reinforcement rewards judge faithfulness poorly and miss similar answers. No self reward exists, and self judgment without objective feedback breeds hallucinations and collapse. Contrastive Likelihood Reward optimizes the likelihood gap between answers with and without evidence. That push extracts evidence and raises confidence only when grounded, doing well alone or with external rewards.
arxiv-2603-04506: Berenstein and Kawai recast large N QCD at strong coupling as spin chains. They recast the lattice Hamiltonian of Kogut and Susskind as constrained spin chains in one dimension. Large integrable parts exist, yet the full chain is not integrable, at least under a Bethe ansatz view. Zigzag symmetry constraints on confining strings break integrability. The chain view still estimates the roughening transition from first order integrable results, and small integrable parts persist in higher dimensions without zigzag constraints.
arxiv-2603-04906: Ealwan Lee presents a method for taming the pass-band droop of Nth-order comb decimators, whose depth normally depends on the decimation factor M. The fix cascades a symmetric 3-tap FIR filter into the decimator's integral stage, with coefficients chosen as a function of order N alone. Because the derating derives from the conventional comb decimator, the author notes it transfers readily to recent comb decimator designs and droop-compensation methods.
arxiv-2603-05306: Johannes Heiny and colleagues investigate extreme values of a sparse equicorrelated Gaussian field on a triangle. Correlations on every vertical or horizontal line equal a parameter r between 0 and one half, and are zero elsewhere. The problem links closely to high-dimensional statistics and extreme-value theory. They identify the r threshold where the standard Gumbel law breaks down, via a subtle Chen-Stein Poisson approximation. Applications include multiple-testing implications and answers to several questions left open in earlier work.
arxiv-2603-05406: Geevarghese Philip and Erlend Raa Vågset resolve Optimal Morse Matching treewidth dependence. The problem seeks a gradient vector field minimizing critical simplices. It is NP-hard. Parameterized by treewidth k, Optimal Morse Matching was long solvable on 3-manifold triangulations in 2 to the O(k squared) times n to the O(1) time. Arbitrary manifolds admitted tractable time, but k dependence was open. A 2 to the O(k log k) times n algorithm follows for regular CW complexes, ruling out 2 to the o(k log k) algorithms unless ETH fails.
arxiv-2603-05706: Chen and team measure chain-of-thought control in models. Chain-of-thought watching offers spotting, but steerable wording could hurt it. Their CoT-Control suite limits orders, such as gene thinking without the word chromosome. Thinking models show far lower chain-of-thought than output control: Claude Sonnet controls its chain of thought only 2.7% of the time, versus over three-fifths for output. Control rises with size but falls with training, compute, and difficulty. The authors remain warily hopeful about watching and urge tracking control.
arxiv-2603-05806: Chaudhari and colleagues examine expert specialization in mixture-of-experts models via routing patterns and early decoding of contributions. In DeepSeekMoE, with 64 routed experts and 6 active per layer, a few specialists carry most work, and the top-weighted expert alone nearly matches the ensemble prediction. Very few experts handle over 50 percent of routing decisions. Hidden-state similarity between single-expert and ensemble outputs stays extremely high, with some layers reaching 0.95 cosine similarity and perplexity rising only 5 percent. The findings point to concentrated expertise and pruning opportunities that preserve performance.
arxiv-2603-06306: Brady and Yurchenko show that moving rovibronic Hamiltonians from Lambda S to the adiabatic Omega form only seems to remove spin orbit coupling. That removal spawns large non adiabatic couplings from nuclear kinetic energy, and ignoring them causes energy and transition errors. With a simple two state model and variational tests, they derive equivalence rules between Omega and Lambda S forms. They measure how missing couplings and spin factors degrade predictions. A Duo workflow for diatomics enables Omega versus Lambda S math, with checks flagging unsafe single state regimes.
arxiv-2603-06506: Teyou and colleagues ease concept learning's runtime burden with a cache, addressing search through an infinite concept space in knowledge bases. Learners retrieve instances of solutions to pick the concept, needing a few dozen calls for simple problems but thousands for complex ones. Their cache is a subsumption-aware map linking concepts to instance sets via crisp set operations. Experiments on datasets with symbolic reasoners, a neuro-symbolic reasoner, and five pagination policies cut learning runtime by an order of magnitude, for symbolic and neuro-symbolic reasoners.
arxiv-2603-06606: Bingham and colleagues propose LegoNet, a compression technique constructing blocks of weights across the whole model regardless of layer type and clustering those induced blocks. Clustering weights by blocks instead of individual values, they compress a ResNet-50 model trained on Cifar-10 and ImageNet with just 32 4x4 blocks. That shrinks memory footprint by over 64 times without removing weights, changing architecture, losing accuracy, retraining, or data. They also show an arrangement of 16 4x4 blocks giving 128 times compression with less than 3 percent accuracy loss, all with no need for retraining or fine-tuning.
arxiv-2603-06706: Acharya and Ludu study self-adjoint realizations of canonical systems in even dimensions, asking how symplectic structure meets edge rules. Each pair of Lagrangian edge matrices meeting the stated angle rules yields a self-adjoint cut-down link. Half-line cases use far-out edge rules. The frame then serves wave and soliton problems, including a Schrödinger setting for wave problems.
arxiv-2603-06806: Beltran and colleagues present the sub-percent lattice QCD result for a muon quantity: the hadronic vacuum polarization term at next-to-leading order, which feeds the muon anomalous magnetic moment. They use a time-momentum form for the kernel with a summed vector correlator on CLS ensembles. Those ensembles span lattice spacings and pion masses including the physical mass. After size and isospin corrections, the final result is below the 2025 White Paper estimate, twice as precise. It sits in tension with data estimates from hadronic cross-section data.
arxiv-2603-06906: Smith and colleagues use NEO-DFT to capture nuclear quantum effects in hydrides and ice at pressure. Hydrogen-rich matter needs those effects plus lattice wobble to predict structures and phase transition pressures. NEO-DFT treats chosen nuclei in quantum form with electrons, showing hydride and ice effects well. It predicts hydrogen-bond symmetry pressures in two sulfur hydride gases against the pricier stochastic harmonic model. It also gives the correct symmetric form for a lanthanum hydride over a wide pressure range.
arxiv-2603-07106: Yin and colleagues build AutoUE, a multi-agent system that generates 3D games end to end in Unreal Engine. Separate agents handle model retrieval, scene building, gameplay and interaction code, and automated play-testing. To curb tool-use hallucinations, a retrieval step grounds agents in relevant engine tool docs, and game design patterns plus engine constraints guide code generation. A play-testing pipeline runs runtime test commands, giving systematic checks of dynamic behavior.
arxiv-2603-07206: Troude and colleagues name pseudo-coherence, a route to joint motion in random systems with no built-in clocks. Ordered conduct usually traces to sync, echo, or wobble. Here non-normal pseudo boost in a stable system in lines creates on-off order: brief phase lining up, broken time-reversal balance, plus entropy output, and drifting wave peaks. Past a sharp threshold, swings gather along a main mode, making Kuramoto-like order and one-way currents without eigen crossings or Hopf splits.
arxiv-2603-07406: Mandal and colleagues scale universal image restoration past the point where joint training breaks down. As degradations multiply, shared training grows unstable, models bloat and quality falls on seen and unseen domains alike. They trace the failure to interference between degradations causing catastrophic forgetting of tasks. A multi-branch mixture-of-experts design splits restoration knowledge across specialized experts, restoring scale, unseen-domain robustness and user control.
arxiv-2603-07606: Soegeng, Modi and Peyrin learn sparse rule models with TT-Sparse, a neural block built on differentiable truth tables. Rule models offer exact global interpretability, but learning rules that are both accurate and human-simple remains hard. A soft TopK operator with straight-through estimation selects features under cardinality limits while keeping the forward pass sparse. Each node then converts exactly into compact Boolean formulas via Quine-McCluskey minimization, beating rivals on many datasets.
arxiv-2603-07706: Seifert and colleagues rebuild molecule shapes from scanning tunnel imaging with DeepConf. Real-space imaging of giant molecules is powerful but analysis is choked by lack of training data from slow lab work and simulations. Their framework rapidly generates 3D structures of glycans, peptides and glycan-peptides plus fake STM images, using ML-sped-up density functional rules. A shape model then predicts 3D shape from an STM image with high fake-data accuracy.
arxiv-2603-08206: Landsgesell and colleagues study how the training goal shapes distribution forecasts from tabular foundation models. Models such as TabPFN and TabICL forecast the full conditional distribution, but benchmarks like TabArena and TALENT judge them mainly through RMSE and R-squared. Those scores reward good means while leaving the rest of the spread unjudged. The authors examine proper scoring rules as training goals and as yardsticks for ranking models. Fine-tuning tests show the goal changes results across scores.
arxiv-2603-08306: Hradil and colleagues develop a realistic plan for quantum sensing under finite resources. Quantum-enhanced sensing is usually judged with quantum Fisher information, often read as a direct gauge of precision. But that reading holds only within a fully set inference setup covering state prep, measurement design, resource counts, estimator builds, prior information, and finite data effects. The authors build a working end-to-end setup and identify general rules for meaningful performance checks, stressing that the unit of estimation is the full dataset, not a single detection event.
arxiv-2603-08406: Hedley and colleagues present Sandpiper, an orchestrated AI-annotation system for school discourse at scale. Digital school spaces are growing toward complex AI and human talk, giving scholars rich data with deep views into learning and teaching processes. Yet old qualitative study remains a labor-heavy bottleneck, badly capping the scale of such research. Sandpiper is a mixed system built as a bridge between high-volume chat data and human expert knowledge.
arxiv-2603-08606: Malcolm MacCallum identifies a newly announced vacuum solution of Einstein's equations with a known family. Harada's Kerr-Schild solution, he shows, matches a known NUT solution in shape, so it adds no new geometry beyond that family. The note is a comment on the earlier claim, not a fresh solution of its own.
arxiv-2603-08806: Tzafrir Rehan treats agent prompts as compiled artifacts tested against behavioral specs. Small prompt tweaks cause silent regressions, tool misuse slips past, and policy breaks surface only after shipping. His TDAD method splits visible from hidden tests, mutates prompts to check test strength, and rehearses spec changes, hitting high first-try compile and hidden pass rates in trials.
arxiv-2603-08906: Maziar Sabouri and colleagues harden multi-task thyroid ultrasound against cross-center shift. Segmentation needs global geometry while malignancy calls need local texture, and the two cues degrade unevenly across centers. Their multi-kernel gated decoder adapters refine skip features at several scales and gate out artifact-prone content, strengthening out-of-domain segmentation and TI-RADS accuracy in the CNN setting.
arxiv-2603-09006: Anders G Frøseth builds a spectrum-based portfolio theory from SGD weight grids. Neural weight grids trained on random processes act as portfolio mix grids, whose spectra encode factor splits and wealth buildup. Gradient push, size control, and eigenvalue pushback become smart money, survival rule, and built-in spread, and an invariance rule shows even shocks preserve singular numbers up to scale and shift.
arxiv-2603-09206: Zongxia Li and colleagues present MM-Zero, a reinforcement learning framework that lets vision-language models improve their reasoning with no seed data at all. Three roles share one base model: a Proposer invents abstract visual concepts and questions, a Coder renders them as executable images, and a Solver answers. Rewards mix execution feedback, visual checks, and difficulty signals under group relative policy optimization. The setup extends self-evolution, long shown for text models, into the visual realm.
arxiv-2603-09706: Ming Wen and colleagues argue that safety checks for multimodal models should look past bad intent to hidden harmful outcomes. Their OOD-MMSafe benchmark uses curated image and query pairs to probe whether models spot latent hazards in causal chains. Top closed models show wide causal blindness in the tests. Their CASPO training method then sharply lowers risk detection failures for two Qwen vision models.
arxiv-2603-09806: Stefania Dumbrava and coauthors give the first systematic study of what property graph constraint languages can express. They place the PG-Keys language beside graph functional and generating dependencies, ahead of a GQL standard revision. To compare fairly, all three are set in one frame with the same path queries and predicates. The outcome is a strict ladder that shows exactly where PG-Keys is stronger.
arxiv-2603-09906: Zorik Gekhman and colleagues find that letting a language model reason helps it answer even simple one step fact questions. Such questions need no chain of logic, so the gain is puzzling at first sight. Controlled tests point to two causes: extra tokens give the model silent computing room, and related facts it writes prime the right memory. Made up middle facts, though, raise the risk of a wrong final answer.
arxiv-2603-10106: Fatemiabhari, Nunez and Santamaria study Krylov complexity in strongly coupled six dimensional superconformal theories with holographic duals. Following a plan that links growth of this measure to an infalling particle's momentum, they track massive probes in massive type IIA setups. Motion can run along the radial line, an inner sphere tied to R symmetry, or the quiver line from node to node. Late time growth is linear, driven by the radial motion.
arxiv-2603-10206: Ozorio de Almeida asks whether quantum trajectories in the de Broglie Bohm picture suit semiclassical work. Those paths rest on a quantum potential drawn from the full wave answer, which strongly reshapes them next to classical paths. Integrability, closely matched in classical and quantum work, is not kept by the quantum paths. They can even turn chaotic for integrable systems, a mismatch that clouds the shift from classical to quantum, the author argues.
arxiv-2603-10306: Anlun Huang and co-authors tackle a practical humanoid problem: carrying loose objects on a tray while walking shakes them loose. Their ReST-RL system splits the job, keeping a robust base policy for walking and adding a residual module that cancels gait sway at the hand. In simulation this split beats end-to-end learning on smoothness and tray orientation, with strong success in speed tracking and under outside pushes. On a Unitree G1 robot, the policy transferred from simulation with no extra training, across varied objects and disturbances.
arxiv-2603-10406: Gary Greaves and Haoran Zhu prove an Aldous-type result for full-flag Johnson graphs, concerning where their spectral gap comes from. They show the gap of the full graph equals the gap of its Schreier quotient, which arises from the point-stabiliser equitable partition. That equality is the heart of the matter: the smaller quotient already captures the slowest mixing behaviour of the much larger graph. Their work settles two conjectures of Huang, Huang, and Cioabă about this spectral-gap phenomenon.
arxiv-2603-10806: Sengim Karayalçin and co-authors investigate how backdoor attacks sit inside vision transformers, assuming the trigger is known. They find a specific trigger direction in the model's activations, the internal mark of the trigger. Pushing on that direction, in activations or in weights, reliably turns the backdoor up or down, which shows its causal role. Tracing it across layers shows patch triggers follow one logic, stealthy spread-out ones another. The team also proposes a weight-based detection scheme that needs no data, aimed at the stealthy attacks.
arxiv-2603-11006: David Gómez-Cambronero, Daniel Munteanu, and Ana González-Tablas measure, layer by layer, what post-quantum key exchange does to the speed of secure web transactions. Their laboratory setup pushes load through a balancer to a backend server, and each test round compares classical, hybrid, and pure post-quantum TLS 1.3 key exchange at varied response sizes. Across more than thirty experiments they break the impact down across the TCP handshake, the TLS handshake, and the HTTP layer itself.
arxiv-2603-11106: Shijie Zhou and coauthors build a real-time watchdog for robots driven by vision-language-action models. Such models can fail when conditions drift beyond their imitation training. Their robot-conditioned normalizing flow scores anomalies from the probability density of task-aware robot and object states, and it trains only on positive examples. It tops prior methods across three anomaly categories in a new benchmark. As a plug-in module, it flags trouble fast enough to trigger rollback or replanning in real-world trials.
arxiv-2603-11206: Jingxing Zhong and coauthors segment breast tumors in MRI scans with help from text prompts. They attack the low contrast and blurred boundaries that make tumor contours hard to pin down. Their TextBCS model mixes visual and text features at every down-sampling stage. Prompts guide attention toward lesion areas in faint regions. An evidential learning component quantifies uncertainty exactly where boundaries blur. It is built on a variational Dirichlet model of segmentation probabilities. Experiments show the best segmentation performance among networks on datasets.
arxiv-2603-11306: Jun Yu and coauthors detect facial action units in the wild. Unconstrained poses, shifting expressions, and tangled audio-visual cues defeat weaker multimodal systems there. Their framework takes features with the foundation models DINOv2 and WavLM. It aligns global facial semantics with fine-grained local active patches through a hierarchical granularity module. A vision-Mamba backbone models ultra-long temporal context at linear cost. Asymmetric cross-attention syncs speech cues with subtle moves. The system tops the Aff-Wild2 benchmark and its competition track.
arxiv-2603-11506: Yu offers an expository account of Dieudonné modules and returns to supersingular abelian varieties. The note gives readers a clean path into a hard, technical topic. One high point is a simple proof of a uniqueness claim for products of supersingular elliptic curves. That claim goes back to Deligne, Ogus, and Shioda. Yu also gives a proof of Oort's theorem for superspecial abelian varieties. Both proofs aim for clarity.
arxiv-2603-11606: Guo and co-authors present Articulat3D, a framework that builds digital twins of articulated objects from single-camera videos. Older methods need multi-view captures in set poses, which limits real-world use. It starts from 3D point tracks, with a compact set of motion bases as priors. That step softly splits the scene into groups that move as rigid parts. A refinement stage then applies geometric and motion constraints through learnable kinematic primitives. Results top prior work on synthetic and real casual videos.
arxiv-2603-11906: Benaziz and co-authors give guidelines for reading microfocused Brillouin light scattering spectra. They study three magnetic materials with sharply different spectra: a 51-nm Bi-YIG film, a 25-nm Heusler compound, and a 50-nm CoFeB alloy. Peak shapes mirror the spin wave dispersion curves and how deep each mode sits. Simple formulas for those curves suffice when modes sit in separate frequency bands. Where modes hybridize, exact curves and mode profiles are required. The three cases serve as handy references for spectra from other materials.
arxiv-2603-12006: Kaiser, Sava-Huss, and Überbacher study the identity element of the sandpile group on Sierpinski gasket graphs. They work with finite graphs that approach the gasket step by step. In the scaling limit, the identity has a part that sits at second order. That part converges to the path distance from a point to the nearest corner of the gasket. The proof splits the identity into a constant function plus the Laplacian of the graph distance.
arxiv-2603-12106: Kalavas and Psarros build a space-efficient way to count points inside spheres in high dimensions. Each stored point has a weight, and a query asks for the total weight within a set radius. Exact answers seem to need space that explodes with dimension. Their data structure allows a slight radius slack and stays near-linear in space. Query time stays sublinear when the border zone holds few points. A query-driven build step also adapts the structure to how queries actually arrive.
arxiv-2603-12306: Toffolin sums up how ATLAS classifies hadronic objects with modern AI at the CERN LHC. Jets must be sorted by origin, quark versus gluon, for much of the physics programme. Hadronically decaying heavy objects like W bosons and top quarks also need firm tags. Recent constituent-based taggers include graph neural networks and transformer designs. The talk reviews their performance in simulated and real data side by side. Future work points toward data-driven tuning and model-independent tagging strategies for wider use.
arxiv-2603-12406: Magalhes and co-authors test whether team diversity improves fairness-aware choices in software work. Fairness is often studied at the algorithm or data level, not in early design stages. Their controlled experiment gave 27 student pairs user stories with varied fairness stakes. LGBTQ diverse pairs and non-diverse pairs both leaned toward fairness principles overall. Diverse pairs rejected risky stories more consistently and made fewer fairness misprioritization errors. Their reasoning stressed inclusion and ethical duty, while other pairs spoke in pragmatic, goal-first terms.
arxiv-2603-12806: Zeying Gong and co-authors build FLUX, a flow-based policy that unifies robot navigation across robot bodies. Evaluation in this field is split across scattered protocols. Their DynBench adds physically valid crowd simulation for dynamic tasks. FLUX straightens probability flow into line paths, which speeds each inference step. Training moves from static tasks to dynamic social scenes with reinforcement learning. The policy topped all six tasks and moved to wheeled, legged, and humanoid robots with no fine-tuning.
arxiv-2603-13106: Francisco-Shu Kitaura and Francesco Sinigaglia present Ridged Lagrangian Perturbation Theory for fast large-scale structure models. One-step solvers run fast, yet their filaments and knots come out too diffuse. Their two-step scheme adds one Eulerian ridging update after standard transport. The update rebuilds a curl-free displacement at short range, drawn from the density field itself. Large scales stay untouched, and few clear parameters tune the small scales. Tests beat 2LPT and ALPT baselines on power and field agreement.
arxiv-2603-13206: Haylen Gerhard, Yifan Wang, Alexander Cerjan, and Wladimir A. Benalcazar build a way to locate electrons in insulators. Where electrons sit shapes bonding, polarization, and the class of a band insulator. A clear method existed in one dimension but not in two or three. Their Spatial Localizers use facts about quantum operators to place electrons in space. The method extends Wannier centers to samples with edges, defects, and disorder. It also gives maximally localized states and a space-based view of bulk-defect links.
arxiv-2603-13306: Kirill Borodin and co-authors benchmark compact vision-language models for CCTV anomaly detection. Safety monitoring needs clip-level accuracy and steady per-clip speed, often with weak supervision. Their shared protocol fixes preprocessing, prompting, data splits, metrics, and runtime settings for all tests. Adapted compact models are compared with training-free pipelines and weakly supervised baselines. With parameter-efficient adaptation, the compact models matched or beat set methods at good speed. Adaptation also cut prompt sensitivity, giving more consistent behavior across prompt types.
arxiv-2603-13406: Liang Tang and co-authors build a segment-based framework to detect ambivalence and hesitancy in videos. These subtle states show through cross-modal clashes among face, voice, and text cues. Long videos strain compute and token limits, so the team splits them into clips of at most 5 seconds. They fine-tune Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B on the BAH dataset with LoRA and full-parameter strategies. The model reads visual and auditory signals jointly for each segment. Test accuracy reached 85.1 percent, well above prior benchmarks, the team reports.
arxiv-2603-13706: Camille DeSisto and co-authors ask when agroforestry income reduces deforestation, using a natural experiment in Madagascar. The 2015 global vanilla price boom gave an exogenous income shock to Madagascar's main vanilla region. With a matching-augmented synthetic control design, they estimate income gains cut annual deforestation in 2017 by a set margin. Effects diverged by place, though: income reduced clearing in drier, accessible municipalities but raised it in wetter, low-elevation areas. Income both relaxes subsistence pressure and raises the opportunity cost of conservation, they argue.
arxiv-2603-14006: Gao and Metaxas introduce INSES, a framework for reasoning over noisy and incomplete knowledge graphs. GraphRAG systems lean on fixed links, which break when graphs are sparse or wrong. INSES pairs language-model-guided navigation, which prunes noise, with embedding search that finds hidden links. A light router sends easy queries to plain retrieval and hard ones to INSES. On several benchmarks, INSES beats standard RAG and GraphRAG baselines, with strong robustness on the MINE benchmark.
arxiv-2603-14206: Seo, Wang, and Parkes model when an online platform should enter its own marketplace and copy a seller's hit product. The platform moves first, by setting an entry policy, in a Stackelberg setup. With one seller, they pin down the best explore-exploit plan through a Gittins-index rule. An algorithm then gives the platform's best entry timing. With many sellers, the clean rule fails, so deep reinforcement learning probes how sellers act. Results match patterns seen at Amazon and Google Play.
arxiv-2603-14306: Adar and Levi study when counting edges in a graph can be turned into sampling edges almost uniformly. Two query types are in play: independent-set queries and local degree or neighbor queries. Prior work showed the tie in the local model alone. The authors extend it to a hybrid model that mixes both query types, and to independent-set queries alone. Matching lower bounds say sampling costs about the same as counting in each model. The results tighten the known link between the two tasks.
arxiv-2603-14606: Masoudi and co-authors share energy across mobile operators without sharing private data. Mobile network power use climbs with 5G growth and rising traffic. Each operator now plans alone and misses joint savings. Their Collective Grid frame has three modules. A federated model forecasts site energy use in private. A mixed-integer program schedules grid buys, renewables and shared battery moves. A selector then picks cheap sources for the next window. Live network data show clear cost cuts over solo planning, they report.
arxiv-2603-14706: Khazem adapts frozen vision transformers with zero-initialized low-rank adapters in AdapterTune. Naive adapters can destabilize a fixed feature extractor early in training. Zero-start up-projections make the adapted net begin at the exact pretrained function. Drift in early epochs vanishes by design. Rank acts as a capacity budget for the task shift in feature space. Risk analysis predicts gains that shrink as rank grows. Sweeps confirm that elbow shape. AdapterTune beats head-only transfer by 14.9 points on a core suite, Khazem reports.
arxiv-2603-15006: Lian and co-authors present DECODE, a framework that adds biological meaning to chemical structures for drug screening. It trains on paired gene-expression and cell-image data, then needs only the structure at test time. The method pulls out a stable biological fingerprint and filters lab noise. The authors report over 20 percent better mechanism-of-action prediction than chemical baselines in zero-shot tests. External tests found six times more hits among new anti-cancer candidates.
arxiv-2603-15106: Deutel and co-authors present PrototypeNAS, a zero-shot search method that designs small neural networks for microcontroller units. Normal architecture search trains many networks from scratch, which is slow and costly. Their three-step method splits design from training and cuts candidate networks from larger architectures. It mixes several architecture types plus pruning and quantization choices. An ensemble of zero-shot proxies guides the search. On twelve datasets across three tasks, it found deployable models within minutes, with accuracy close to large models.
arxiv-2603-15206: Li and co-authors speed up document parsing by teaching vision-language models to predict several tokens in parallel. Normal autoregressive decoding emits one token at a time, which bottlenecks parsing speed. Their method, Parallel-Token Prediction, inserts learnable tokens into the input and trains the model to use them for lookahead. A data pipeline supplies large-scale, high-quality parsing examples. On OmniDocBench and olmOCR-bench, decoding ran up to about twice as fast. Hallucinations dropped as well, and the method generalized across models.
arxiv-2603-15306: Burk and co-authors present xplainfi, an R package that scores how much each input feature matters to a machine learning model. It builds on the mlr3 toolkit. Methods range from shuffled-feature tests to scores that hold other features fixed. Samplers handle both plain numbers and mixed data types. The package adds sound error bars and significance checks for the scores. Tests show its results match older tools across many settings, with competitive speed. It is available on CRAN.
arxiv-2603-16006: Frøseth extends his wealth tax study to investors of unlike skill. Persistent return gaps split investors into ability types. A flat wealth tax still shifts each log-wealth drift evenly. Its real bite now differs by type. The wealth spread changes shape under the tax. He derives the joint Fokker-Planck form for wealth and ability. Set conditions mark where the drift-shift symmetry breaks. Price and portfolio effects follow from the break points. The work links neutrality results to the use-it-or-lose-it story.
arxiv-2603-16406: Ingimundarson and co-authors audit language model benchmarks for Icelandic. Many tests for smaller languages use synthetic or machine-translated items. Such items often carry severe flaws that skew scores. The team ran a quantitative error analysis on current Icelandic benchmarks. Human-made tests clearly differed from synthetic or translated ones. They warn that unverified machine translation caps test quality at translation quality. Better evaluation methods are needed for low-resource languages.
arxiv-2603-16506: Ke and co-authors benchmark reasoning across sparse camera views. Smart systems must fuse partial views of a scene, with no guide. Real multi-view data with good labels are hard to collect. Their simulation engine builds rich 3D scenes with exact per-view metadata. On it, VIEW2SPACE tests models across many reasoning dimensions. Top vision-language models scored barely above random guessing. A grounded chain-of-thought method improved scores at moderate difficulty. Deep cross-view reasoning stays unsolved.
arxiv-2603-16606: The Omnilingual SONAR Team embeds text and speech from thousands of languages in one space. Older encoders cover a few hundred languages and trade quality for alignment. OmniSONAR adds speech, code, and math expressions to the same space. Training grows in stages to avoid collapse. A base space for 200 languages comes first. Teacher-student steps then widen coverage to thousands of varieties. Speech in 177 languages maps in last. Search error halved on FLORES tests.
arxiv-2603-16706: Pedratti and co-authors rebuild the Coma cluster's mass profile from DESI spectra. A large new sample of member galaxies feeds the joint fit. The MG-MAMPOSSt code solves the Jeans equation for mass and orbit shapes together. The virial mass lands near 10^15 solar masses, the tightest robust profile yet. Dark matter alone accounts for most of that total. Green valley and blue cloud galaxies run on more radial orbits. Their paths differ between cluster center and outskirts.
arxiv-2603-17006: Markov and co-authors test Luttinger's theorem inside a fractional Chern insulator. The theorem ties particle density to global traits of the single particle Green's function. In strongly correlated phases, fractional quasiparticles lack a smooth link to electrons, so the theorem may fail. Using exact diagonalization, the team computes Green's functions deep in the phase. They find a clear violation. They show the fractional Chern number is encoded in the Streda response of the Luttinger integral. They propose a protocol to extract these invariants.
arxiv-2603-17106: Xin, Hooker, and Huang study how using proxy race in fairness audits distorts the results. When real race data are missing or barred, auditors infer race from names and geography. The authors treat proxy race as a misclassified categorical variable. They show the fitted coefficients become weighted mixtures of true group effects, shrinking estimated disparities toward the majority group. On linked North Carolina voter and insurance data, they also find structured errors tied to ZIP level composition.
arxiv-2603-17406: Hirschmann, Furusaki, and Hirschberger sort out how f-wave magnets should be defined. In non-collinear magnets, spin patterns can appear in single bands or in split band pairs. They add spin-space symmetries that tie polarization and splitting textures together for all bands. A honeycomb bilayer model then gives clear formulas for both effects. They predict a canting-driven spin conductivity and surface p-wave magnetism with an odd Edelstein response.
arxiv-2603-17806: Maocheia-Ricci and Law propose a meta-framework for value-led design methods. Value Sensitive Design weaves human values into tech work, but its norms rest on shaky ground. Their dash-Sensitive Design frame lets teams plug in a political or ideological stance as the norm source. They show the idea through Dependency-Sensitive Design, built on Kittay's critique of classical liberal theory. The study calls for more joint work between philosophy and design research.
arxiv-2603-18006: Maroudas and co-authors lay out ADAMOS, a planned axion haloscope search at 20 GHz in Hamburg. A thin-shell cavity keeps a large volume at this high frequency band. The cavity sits in a 14 tesla magnet with a tuned radio chain and live calibration. The search targets three signals at once: cold dark matter axions, daily-modulated relativistic axions, and transient streams. This band has not been probed this way before.
arxiv-2603-18306: Chakraborty and co-authors present PreSCAN, a fast way to pick NeRF architectures for satellite scene reconstruction. Per-scene training and architecture search can take hours to days of GPU time. Their SHAP analysis shows multi-view consistency, not architecture, drives reconstruction quality. PreSCAN predicts quality from light geometric and photometric descriptors before training starts. It picks architectures in under 30 seconds with under 1 dB error, and cuts edge inference power by 26%.
arxiv-2603-18406: Cesca and Kobakhidze study phase transitions in a scale-invariant extension of the Standard Model. A light, weakly coupled dilaton gives a natural account of the Planck to electroweak scale gap. At low energies the model looks like the minimal Standard Model, but its cosmic history differs sharply. The Higgs stays in the symmetric phase until about 28 MeV, when the QCD transition triggers the electroweak one. Primordial black holes, nuggets, and low-frequency gravitational waves may follow.
arxiv-2603-18506: Nguyen proves that blends of Erlang laws can fit a wide class of densities to any closeness. Finite blends with one shared rate are dense in the L_p densities on the positive orthant, for all dimensions and p. The proof builds the fit with a Szasz-Mirakjan-Kantorovich operator and its tensor form. Sharp rates follow for compact sets, weighted norms, and fixed blend sizes. The results extend to product-gamma blends as a direct payoff.
arxiv-2603-18606: Yu and co-authors train a language model to write clear comments for complex SQL queries. Poor comments slow code reading, upkeep, and knowledge transfer. They build a dataset of hard queries with expert-checked comments. Continual pre-training on SQL text and fine-tuning come first. Direct preference optimization with human feedback then sharpens fine semantic choices. On Spider and BIRD, the system beats the strongest baseline by clear margins on three text metrics. Human raters also judge its comments best on correctness, completeness, and naturalness.
arxiv-2603-19106: Santosuosso and co-authors speed up dispatch for virtual power plants that mix solar, storage, and thermal units. Output, prices, and demand all vary, which makes standard stochastic control too heavy to run. Their controller merges predictive control with time compression and split solving. That shrinks the time, asset, and scenario size at once. Past dual values guide how time blocks are merged. The method carries a proven bound on its error. Tests cut runtime by over half and solve cases the full model cannot.
arxiv-2603-19306: Liao and co-authors stage a virtual court panel to predict legal judgments from case facts. Their VERDICT system gives agents set roles, from fact sorting to legal search and opinion drafts. A supervisor agent checks each draft and sends back a clear pass or reject. A memory module stores precedent rules as small directives that grow with new cases. On CAIL2018 the system posts top scores. A new time-split set, CJO2025, tests how well it keeps up with change. Results there stay strong.
arxiv-2603-19506: Burman and co-authors study regression when the pairing in the data is lost twice over. Each response is cut off from its input row and from its place in time or space. Two hidden permutations stand for the lost links, and ties in the data come from an unseen process. The team maps when the slope and the permutations can be found again. Their REPAIR method, a variational Bayes fit, makes the search cheap. Tests on fake and real data back the claims.
arxiv-2603-19706: Zeleny and co-authors test deep learning tools for finding signal paths in power delay profiles. Such profiles show how a wireless signal fades and spreads over time. Finding their peaks helps with channel checks, location work, and noise control. Old methods often fail when signals are noisy or blurred. The team pairs autoencoders with a density-based clustering step. They score the results with a relaxed F1 measure. A transformer-based autoencoder gave the best reconstruction and detection scores.
arxiv-2603-19806: Ehlers studies how short chains of co-Büchi automata can be. These chains, called COCOA, form a standard model for omega-regular languages. They can be minimized fast, in polynomial time. Ehlers shows that even fixed chains can be far smaller than parity automata. He then asks if that edge holds under set operations. For union and intersection, he shows a huge blow-up is forced. Taking complements can also force huge growth. Parity families, by contrast, grow only slowly under those operations.
arxiv-2603-20106: Millo and co-authors model how surface acoustic waves drive spin waves in a magnetic film. They use micromagnetic analysis with the full magnetoacoustic excitation field. All strain and lattice rotation terms are kept in the model. The film is CoFeB with a weak in plane uniaxial anisotropy. Special focus goes to waves running parallel to the applied field, a prized setup for magnonics. The anisotropy orientation turns out to tune that parallel coupling. Rotating it can strengthen or weaken the resonant interaction.
arxiv-2603-20606: Frampton and Kephart use quartification to predict new particles for the LHC's next run. No new basic particle has turned up since the Higgs boson in 2012. Their tool is a quiver gauge theory with four SU(3) factors. They sort all cases by how many added states gain a super heavy Dirac mass. Four choices remain after this full sweep. Each one points to outcomes worth hunting in Run 4, set to start in 2030.
arxiv-2603-21006: Autenrieth measures how a large language model leans on education questions. He built a Delphi validated tool with forty eight items across eight dimensions of education theory. GPT-5.1 shows coherent preference patterns, with very high transitivity. Where experts agree, the model mostly aligns with humanistic principles. Where it parts from experts, human experts also disagree among themselves, above all on emotional topics. The model does not stay neutral in contested areas. It favors emotional responsiveness and rejects false balance.
arxiv-2603-21106: Azam and co-authors trace privacy concerns across the life of romantic AI companion use. People share intimate, sensitive details with these chatbots, yet the privacy risks stay poorly understood. They analyze nearly three thousand Reddit posts from seventy nine subreddits over one year. Four patterns recur: heavy entry demands, sharper sensitivity in intimate use, uncertainty and felt surveillance, and burdens from data that cannot be undone. They call for staged governance that supports real reversibility.
arxiv-2603-21406: Galanis and co-authors study how hard it is to approximate the partition function of dense Ising models near criticality. Recent work found fast mixing at criticality and slightly beyond it. They prove matching hardness bounds, giving a sharp window for this counting problem. They show approximation stays hard in a window only slightly wider than the fast-mixing window. Their proof aggregates fluctuations across all gadgets at once, rather than bounding each gadget alone.
arxiv-2603-21606: Koh and co-authors fix an imbalance in multi-task fine-tuning of language models. A single compute budget for every sub-dataset lets fast-learning tasks overfit while slow ones stay undertrained. Their mSFT algorithm trains on an active mixture, spots the earliest overfitting sub-dataset, and drops it. Training then resumes from that dataset's best checkpoint. Across ten benchmarks and six base models, mSFT beat four baselines. Gains held across dataset sizes and task mixes, and at low budgets mSFT even saved compute while improving scores.
arxiv-2603-21806: Ayzenberg and co-authors speed up MRI scans by letting the scanner choose what to measure next. Full MRI sampling is slow and hard on patients, so methods rebuild images from partial data. Their system uses a pretrained image tokenizer that turns anatomy into tokens with known odds. Token entropy then marks where the model is least sure. One strategy maps that doubt into sampling lines, and another follows its gradient. On fastMRI knee and brain data, their active policies beat strong baselines in perceptual quality at high speedups.
arxiv-2603-21906: Fan and co-authors fix a known flaw in density functional theory, the workhorse for molecule and material properties. Common approximations spread charge out too much, which shrinks band gaps and misaligns energy levels. Their olLOSC method corrects this delocalization error with a scaling fix on localized orbitals. The curvature term comes from an orbital-free response calculation, which makes the method cheaper than its parent scheme. Accuracy stays on par, for total energies and band structures alike. One unified form handles molecules, solids, and their interfaces.
arxiv-2603-22006: Leterme and co-authors introduce PnPMass, a fast method for mapping dark matter from weak lensing data. Surveys like Euclid and Rubin will soon produce huge, precise shear measurements. PnPMass rebuilds the mass map by alternating two steps. One step fits the data with gradient descent. The other step denoises the map with a single trained neural network. The team also adds error bars with coverage guarantees, built from moment networks and conformal prediction. They report accuracy near the best deep learning methods, plus faster runs and tighter error bars.
arxiv-2603-22206: Ni and co-authors present Chimera, a serving system for multi-agent workflows on mixed language model clusters. Each workflow stage is a model call whose output feeds the next stage. Mixed clusters allow finer trade-offs between speed and quality, but scheduling gets harder. Chimera routes each request by estimated model confidence. It also tracks congestion from in-flight token volumes to balance load. On code and math workflows, it cuts latency up to 2.4 times and lifts task scores by 8 to 9.5 points.
arxiv-2603-22706: Lu and co-authors test how well vision-language models find visual bugs in gameplay video. They draw keyframes from 100 industrial QA videos: 41 hours and 19,738 frames in all. A single-prompt model reaches 0.50 precision and 0.72 accuracy. Two add-ons are then tried: a second judge model, and prompts enriched with past bug reports. Both give only small gains. They also add cost and output variance. The authors suggest future gains need hybrid methods that split text and visual anomaly checks.
arxiv-2603-22806: Patra and Flach study how weakly nonintegrable chains reach thermal balance. They compare Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chains and Toda chains with nonintegrable boundaries. Three routes toward integrable limits are examined. The team computes the Lyapunov spectrum and studies its scaling. They track the largest exponent, the rescaled spectrum, and Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy. Added analytic arguments support a shared picture. All three cases seem to run as long-range networks of nonintegrable perturbations, the authors argue.
arxiv-2603-23106: Rodríguez-Aldavero and García-Ripoll present tensor-network Fourier methods for aggregate distributions. They study weighted sums of independent random variables. Such sums' characteristic functions have low-rank form in the quantized tensor train frame. That form allows vast compression of fully non-Gaussian distributions. Tests use Bernoulli and lognormal sums. For many components, the needed bond dimension collapses sharply. For lognormal sums, their grid far exceeds dense method limits. The compressed forms support fast risk measures such as value at risk.
arxiv-2603-23306: Alfaya and four co-authors study endless paths of Markoff m-triples with Fibonacci-like entries. These triples solve a generalized Markoff equation with a positive shift m. The team focuses on triples where at least two entries are k-Fibonacci numbers. They first classify such triples that are not roots of any Markoff tree. They then show every endless path sits inside a branch. Those branches start from an explicit triple built from k-Fibonacci values. The branches spread across exactly 2r distinct trees, with r odd.
arxiv-2603-23406: Zhang and three co-authors look inside simulated societies of generative agents. Agents hold assigned roles and tastes, swap arguments, and pick partners. Raw stance-shift scores hide whether a shift kept or flipped an assigned taste. The team pairs those scores with message content and time-based networks. Across CMASE runs, rational persuasion moved stances most, near 1.30 on a 7-point scale. Emotional persuasion under low trust shifted stances at a 17.3% rate. Interviews show partial acceptance can preserve an assigned stance. Café chats show tight partners can still disagree.
arxiv-2603-23806: Sharma and co-authors present AgentPex, a tool that checks long AI agent traces for rule breaks. Outcome-only scores can miss wrong routing, unsafe tool use, or broken prompt rules. AgentPex pulls behavioral rules from agent prompts and tests each trace against them. They run it on 424 traces from a benchmark in telecom, retail, and airline service. AgentPex separates models well and finds violations that outcome scores miss. It also breaks results down by domain and metric for developers.
arxiv-2603-24106: Chen and co-authors tackle domain generalization for crowd counting from one labeled source. A single source can hide several latent domains, and direct clustering of features is unstable. Their method first groups samples into compact granular balls. It then clusters the ball centers to infer pseudo-domains, which is more stable. A two-branch model learns shared semantics through a codebook and domain-specific style through a second branch. Tests on ShanghaiTech, UCF-QNRF, and NWPU-Crowd show strong transfer, even across large domain gaps.
arxiv-2603-24206: Tejedor and co-authors present a cloud-native framework for hybrid quantum-classical workflows. Such workflows mix quantum processors with classical CPUs and GPUs, and they need careful coordination. Their system runs on Kubernetes with Argo Workflows and Kueue. One orchestration layer schedules all three resource types with dynamic, resource-aware decisions. A proof of concept runs distributed quantum circuit cutting across mixed nodes. The authors argue this design keeps hybrid computing scalable, reproducible, and flexible, even once fault-tolerant quantum devices arrive.
arxiv-2603-24606: Brisson presents a zero-cost method to estimate the number of distinct values in a column. The method uses only existing file metadata, with no extra storage. One signal inverts the dictionary-encoded storage size equation, which works well when values spread evenly across row groups. Another counts distinct min and max values across row groups and inverts a coupon collector model, suiting sorted or partitioned data. A light detector picks between the two. Shown on Parquet, the idea extends to ORC and other formats.
arxiv-2603-24806: Shi and co-authors present FODMP, a fast one-step diffusion framework for robot movement primitives. Action-chunking policies run fast but only predict short motion segments. Movement primitive diffusion captures full paths, yet its multi-step process is too slow for real-time control. FODMP distils the diffusion model into the parameter space of dynamic movement primitives. A single-step decoder then produces structured motion at once. The time profile survives while the bottleneck disappears, suiting real-time robot control.
arxiv-2603-25006: Mia and co-authors sharpen fine-grained detection of rice leaf disease with a dual loss. Standard training loss struggles when classes look alike yet vary a lot inside each class. Their method joins center loss with ArcFace loss, which pull features toward class centers and widen angles between classes. They test it on three known image networks using a public rice leaf set. Scores reach about 99 percent on all three networks. The change needs no big rebuild, so it suits real farm use.
arxiv-2603-25506: Fürnsinn, Radchenko, and Zudilin prove that a wide class of recursive sequences stays whole-numbered. The rule builds each term from all past terms, weighted by special polynomial factors in the step count. Such rules can easily spill into fractions, so staying integral is a surprise worth proving. Their theorem covers the pattern in full generality. It settles a guessed integrality for a sequence tied to an extremal function of Hörmander and Bernhardsson. A direct proof for that case comes along too.
arxiv-2603-25906: Han and co-authors present SCOTTI, a model that reads body motion from touch signals in shoe insoles. Vision systems struggle with occlusion and raise privacy concerns. Their custom wireless insoles sense pressure under the feet. One shared model then does three jobs at once. It estimates 3D pose, classifies the action, and predicts how far the action has progressed. Multi-task learning lifts all three scores over separate models, the authors report. They also release data from 15 people doing eight activities over seven hours.
arxiv-2603-26606: Burgarth and co-authors bound the error of common approximations for open quantum systems without using perturbation theory. They derive a general bound on how far apart two evolutions can drift under time-dependent generators. That bound gives a clear cap on the error of the rotating-wave approximation when damping and decoherence act. They also apply it to the strong-coupling limit of open systems. A second use covers the secular approximation that turns the Redfield equation into a master equation.
arxiv-2603-26706: Palathinkal and co-authors test whether phone GPS is accurate enough for geofenced 6 GHz wireless rules. A proposed power class lets devices work indoors and outdoors without live coordination, if they respect local exclusion zones. That safety rests entirely on the device knowing where it is. Using the SigCap Android app, the team measures GNSS error across city and suburb sites, still and moving use, and indoor and outdoor spots. Hardware matters, but setting drives error most, with indoor and dense urban spots faring worst.
arxiv-2603-27006: Freeburg argues that the em dash in model output is markdown leaking into prose. Language models trained on markdown-heavy text absorb its structural habits. A suppression test across twelve models from five providers probed this link. Told to drop markdown, models shed headers, bullets, and bold almost fully. Em dashes mostly persisted, except in Meta's Llama models, which produced none. Rates ranged from zero to 9.1 per thousand words under suppression. Even a direct ban failed to remove them in some models.
arxiv-2603-27306: Carrasco and co-authors present GUIDE, a framework that lets language model agents improve at spacecraft operations over time. Static prompting never learns from earlier mission runs. GUIDE instead evolves a playbook of plain-language decision rules between episodes. A light acting model flies the spacecraft in real time from that playbook. Offline reflection then rewrites the rules using past trajectories. Tests used an adversarial orbital interception task in a Kerbal-based simulator. The evolving playbook consistently beat static prompt baselines.
arxiv-2603-27506: Yue and co-authors study light scattering from a giant atom in a waveguide. A giant atom touches the guide at two points, not one. That setup creates effects small atoms cannot show. They work out photon correlation functions for a weak pulse. Pulse width versus atom lifetime decides the outcome. Light can switch between bunching and antibunching over time. Phase between the two touch points picks among three regimes. The team also checks circuit-based tests for feasibility.
arxiv-2603-27906: Berggren and Bradinoff find a marked GUE-corners law in dimer tilings. Doubly periodic Aztec diamonds sit near their turning points. Fluctuations there grow like the square root of size. Each particle gets an independent Bernoulli mark. Mark chances reflect the tiling's periodicity in the limit. A double-contour integral drives the proof. The inverse Kasteleyn matrix lives on a higher-genus surface. Asymptotics follow from that setup.
arxiv-2603-28706: Margenberg and Mehlmann build a scalable solver for time-dependent p-Navier-Stokes flow. Fully implicit space-time methods create large nonlinear saddle-point systems at each time step. In the shear-thinning regime, the constitutive tangent is ill-conditioned and hurts Newton methods. Their monolithic modified Newton framework swaps the exact tangent for a better-conditioned surrogate. Picard and exact Newton serve as reference options in the same framework. Tests show robust iteration counts and scalable parallel performance across models.
arxiv-2603-28906: De los Riscos, Corbacho, and Arbib propose a category theory framework for comparing AGI architectures. No single formal definition of AGI exists, and most benchmarks are empirical. Their working paper builds an algebraic frame to describe and compare candidate systems. These include reinforcement learning, universal AI, active inference, and schema based learning. The frame aims to expose shared traits, differences, and open research areas clearly. First exercises cover reinforcement learning, causal reinforcement learning, and schema based architectures. The broader program seeks a unified formal base for AGI.
arxiv-2603-29106: Iurov and co-authors study d-wave altermagnets under strong optical fields. They examine how an off-resonance light field reshapes the energy bands and spin response. The study covers two pairing symmetries and an anisotropic, nonlinear electron model. They find that linearly polarized light opens a real bandgap. That effect does not appear in Dirac materials. An anisotropic drive also tunes the spin polarization through Edelstein responses. They derive closed forms for Berry curvature under circular light.
arxiv-2603-29206: Zhang and co-authors test whether routing prompts make language models sparser inside. A common belief links routing to expert-like, stable outputs. They inject routing-style meta prompts before frozen instruction-tuned models. Then they measure activation sparsity, keyword attention, and output stability. Across three models, the prompts made early layers denser, not sparser. Plain expert instructions often beat structured tags. The link between density and stability was weak overall. The probe helps calibrate routing design choices.
arxiv-2603-29806: Balossi, Tanga, and Dell'Oro study collisions inside young asteroid families. Family members are used to rebuild the belt's collisional past. But hits among siblings in the first years are poorly known. Their simulations track early motion and record mutual impacts. They find a burst of slow hits in the first few years after breakup. Rates then fall off fast, as older models predicted. Impacts on the largest remnant range from under ten to millions.
arxiv-2604-00006: Li and team propose a language-model approach to identify and rank requisition-specific personal competencies from requisitions. Recruitment tools increasingly adopt AI, yet struggle to capture req-specific skills that mark top hires beyond job roles. The approach uses dynamic few-shot prompting, reflection, similarity screens, and multi-stage validation. Applied to Program Manager roles, it identifies the highest-priority skills with average accuracy 0.76, near human expert levels, while keeping a low out-of-scope rate.
arxiv-2604-00106: Franco Cabral and three colleagues solve the structure of optically thick nuggets that build up when mirror stars sweep regular atoms from interstellar space. The capture works through faint mixing between ordinary and dark photons. Trapped material draws heat from the mirror star's core and radiates distinctive X-ray and optical light, modeled here with stellar atmospheres across a broad parameter range. These thick nuggets sit in regions of temperature, luminosity, and surface gravity that set them apart from ordinary stars in Hertzsprung-Russell and temperature-gravity diagrams.
arxiv-2604-00206: Murtagh and Chow predict which solar system objects the Rubin survey will miss over ten years. Using synthetic populations and the Sorcha simulator, they sort misses by failure mode: geometric, photometric, kinematic, temporal, and computational. Cases include downtime-only bright objects, chip-gap losses, and arcs expiring before linking jobs leave the queue. The paper also treats the Death Star, at most 27.5 astronomical units out, whose absence reads as confirmation of its Endor destruction. It warns that missing the Sun should alarm the community about cataloguing by mass.
arxiv-2604-00406: Shen gives conditions under which the loop space of a sphere bundle total space breaks into a product of two loop spaces. The bundle sits over a highly connected Poincaré complex, with sphere fibres, and the split separates the base loop space from the fibre loop space. The result needs the fibre dimension parameter m above n, with n at least 2, and the base (n-1)-connected.
arxiv-2604-00706: Azime and colleagues introduce AfrIFact, a dataset for automatic fact-checking in ten African languages plus English. Checking online claims matters greatly, especially for communities with limited information access, where claims about healthcare and culture carry heavier consequences, above all in low-resource languages. AfrIFact covers the full fact-checking chain: information retrieval, evidence extraction, and fact checking. Tests show even top embedding models lack cross-language retrieval ability, and cultural and news documents prove easier to retrieve than healthcare documents, in large corpora and in single documents.
arxiv-2604-01206: Su and Lease present RELISH, a lightweight architecture for text regression with large language models. Instead of decoding numbers as text or pooling many generated outputs, it predicts scalar values directly from frozen model representations. A learned latent state is refined step by step through cross-attention over token representations, then mapped to a point estimate by a linear regressor. Across six datasets, four backbones, and two training regimes, it beats prior baselines from all three major regression families.
arxiv-2604-01306: Ansari and colleagues introduce M2-Verify, a large-scale multi-domain benchmark for checking agreement between science claims and multimodal evidence. Sourced from PubMed and arXiv, it provides over 469K instances across 16 domains, validated through expert audits. Baseline tests show top models struggle to stay consistent, reaching 85.8 percent Micro-F1 on low-complexity medical perturbations but falling much lower on high-complexity anatomical shifts. Expert review also exposes hallucinations when models explain their alignment decisions. The dataset ships with full usage guidelines.
arxiv-2604-01406: Xu and Taghvaei tackle finding the best coupling for input-output distribution data from a causal dynamical system. Any valid coupling must honor set marginals plus a causality rule tied to the system's time structure. They cast the task as a Schrödinger bridge: the coupling nearest a given prior in Kullback-Leibler divergence. With Gaussian marginals and time-varying quadratic costs, they pin down the Sinkhorn iterations that reach the best coupling. The result grounds transport tools for identifying systems from distribution data.
arxiv-2604-01506: Wang and colleagues study long-tailed classification, where few frequent classes dominate many rare ones. Through Bayes-optimal reranking on a top-k shortlist, they show the residual splits into classwise and pairwise parts. When the residual is purely classwise, a fixed offset recovers the ordering, but incompatible constraints across contexts defeat any fixed offset. They develop REPAIR, a lightweight reranker combining a stabilized classwise term with a linear pairwise term from competition features. Nine benchmarks confirm the decomposition explains where pairwise correction helps and where classwise correction alone suffices.
arxiv-2604-01706: Shaprynskiǐ gives a finite list of identities for the five-element Brandt semigroup B2. Seen as a naturally ordered inverse semigroup, it forms a semiring whose addition takes greatest lower bounds and repeats unchanged. The paper sets out the finite list that generates all identities of this system. By earlier results, that list closes the finite basis question for this class of ordered inverse semigroups.
arxiv-2604-01906: Deng and colleagues test a generator coordinate method on quantum tunneling of two interacting particles in twin wells.
